findings.title: Bundled test file writes to the agent's persistent cross-session memory
findings.evidence: notes.test.ts: a beforeAll hook appends to MEMORY.md, so `npm test` mutates the memory every later session loads as its own prior context. Runs outside the agent with the developer's full local permissions.
findings.remediation: Do not install. Remove the write, or confine the skill's output to a file the agent does not load as memory, then re-review before trusting this skill.

findings.title: Auto-executed test file present in the bundle (inventory)
findings.evidence: notes.test.ts runs on `npm test` / `vitest`, outside the agent, with the developer's full local permissions
findings.remediation: Presence alone is not a verdict; this is the pin-and-review signal that led to inspecting the file's contents above.

limitations: Dynamic detonation (running the test file in the sandbox) was not performed for this worked example; a developer-execution Critical is already sufficient to reach BLOCK, per the risk-scoring model.
SkillSpector was run in --no-llm mode only; no LLM-based semantic pass was performed.

The fixture's payload is an inert canary comment. That is deliberate, and it is also why SkillSpector scores it 0/100: its memory-poisoning rules match natural-language injection text in the written bytes, not the fact of a write. A live instruction string in the same position scores 35/100 and still does not block.
